claims.text: SELF-FAMILIARITY is a zero-resource, pre-detection self-evaluation method that assesses a language model's familiarity with concepts in an input instruction to withhold responses for unfamiliar concepts.
SELF-FAMILIARITY achieves an AUC of 0.927, an accuracy of 0.868, and an F1 score of 0.854 on Vicuna-13b-v1.3 for hallucinatory instruction classification on the Concept-7 dataset.
SELF-FAMILIARITY achieves an AUC of 0.926, an accuracy of 0.882, and an F1 score of 0.822 on Falcon-7b-instruct for hallucinatory instruction classification on the Concept-7 dataset.
Removing concept grouping from SELF-FAMILIARITY decreases its classification AUC on Vicuna-13b-v1.3 from 0.927 to 0.918.

evidence.description: The authors define SELF-FAMILIARITY as a pre-detection self-evaluation technique evaluating model familiarity with input concepts and withholding generation for unfamiliar concepts under a zero-resource setting.

methodologies.name: SELF-FAMILIARITY
methodologies.description: A zero-resource pre-detection framework consisting of concept extraction, concept guessing via prompt engineering and constrained beam search, and frequency-weighted score aggregation.

limitations.text: Existing post-detection methods identify hallucinations after generation, failing to prevent hallucinated content from occurring initially.
Parameter-based hallucination detection methods suffer from reduced model interpretability compared to chain-of-thought methods.
Models offering API access exclusively cannot be evaluated with SELF-FAMILIARITY due to the requirement for constrained beam search generation control.

future_work.text: Investigate methods to evaluate the language model's understanding of more granular sub-concepts to improve algorithm precision.
